category_title: Adolescents with a history of school failure and mistrust of formal education
minimal_context: The student is asked to complete a reading and writing worksheet during a flexible study period in the Social Guarantee Programme.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please read this text and write down your answers to the questions on the worksheet.

STUDENT: Man, why do we gotta do this? I do not like studying.

TUTOR: It is the assignment for today. Just give it a try and see how far you get.

STUDENT: I don't even get what these words mean. I do not think I am clever enough for this anyway.

TUTOR: Keep trying. Just write down whatever you think is the right answer.

STUDENT: (Pushes the worksheet away) Nah, I'm not doing it. It was easy, but I was not interested in it. I'm not wasting my time on stuff that isn't useful to me.

options.A: Reviews a behavioral contract with the student, outlines the behavior expectations and corresponding rewards, and requires the student to sign it.
options.B: Assesses the student's skills, analyzes their previous study conditions, and evaluates their personal interests, characteristics, and family situation.
options.C: Adheres to a routine and provides positive reinforcement for desired behaviors, such as social praise or stickers on a chart.
options.D: Builds rapport to help the student feel safe, while emphasizing structure, visual cues, predictability, and consistency during the study period.
